newsitem.title: USA: Box Energy says would consider merger bid.
newsitem.headline: Box Energy says would consider merger bid.

text.p: Box Energy Corp would consider a takeover bid but has not received one from Phoenix Canada Oil Co Ltd and is not engaged in talks to sell the company, a Box spokesman said on Tuesday.
"This company has received no offers," spokesman Owen Blicksilver said. "There's been no discussions with anyone in terms of purchase of the company at this time."
Earlier today Phoenix Canada said it planned to make a bid for Box.

Phoenix Canada said it would offer US$12 a share for Box's Class A voting shares, and $11.40 a share for its Class B non-voting shares. Box has 20.8 million shares outstanding -- 3.25 million Class A shares and the rest Class B shares.

Box has been embroiled in what people close to the situation call a family war for control of the company. Tom Box was replaced by his older brother Don as chief executive in August, fueling rumors that the company would be put up for sale.
But Don Box said at the time that there would be no "fire sale" of the company and that he would focus on cutting costs and improving drilling results to boost earnings.
"Box Energy has said it would always consider a legitimate offer but is not seeking offers," Blicksilver said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
On November 14 the Dallas-based company posted a loss of $3.1 million, or $0.15 a share, for the third quarter, compared to earnings of $1.9 million, or $0.09 a share, a year earlier.
Box senior executives were attending the company's annual meeting today in Lafayette, La., and were not immediately available for comment.
